content.text:
Two findings — the second is the real blocker.

## 1. The job never reached Netlify

The build succeeded (4.3 GB, 41,588 pages, 120,415 files, ~2h07m). It died in the **Check site shape** step:

```
sort: write failed: 'standard output': Broken pipe
##[error]Process completed with exit code 2
```

`find ... | sort -rn | head -1` — `head` closes the pipe, `sort` gets SIGPIPE, and `set -o pipefail` turns that into a failed step. Pure shell bug, nothing to do with Netlify. Fixed in [.github/workflows/docs.yml](.github/workflows/docs.yml#L259-L272) by replacing `sort | head` with a single-pass `awk` max (also uses `-exec ... {} +` batching, so it's much faster than the 37s per-`find`-exec version). Verified locally: exits 0.

## 2. The site actually exceeds Netlify's per-directory limit

Running the fixed check against your local dist:

```
largest directory: 77915 ./assets
```

Netlify caps a single directory at **54,000 files**. So once the shape check runs correctly, it will fail — correctly — and the deploy still won't happen. VitePress emits one chunk per page into a flat `assets/`, and at 41.5k pages × locales you're ~44% over.

There's no `build.rolldownOptions.output` config in [docs/.vitepress/config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts#L735) — assets go to the flat default. The fix is to shard `assets/` into subdirectories via `chunkFileNames`/`assetFileNames` functions (e.g. bucket by a hash of the chunk name → ~36 shards of ~2.2k files each).

## On seeding locally

I'd skip it. The seed idea assumed Netlify was rejecting the upload; it never got one byte. And a local seed would mean a ~2h full build plus a 4.3 GB upload over your home connection — slower than the runner, with no benefit, and it can't succeed until the `assets/` sharding lands anyway. Your local dist is also only 1.2 GB (stale/partial), so it isn't a valid seed source as-is.

**Recommendation:** land the shape-check fix plus `assets/` sharding on this branch, merge, and let the workflow do the first real seed. The tradeoff is one more ~2h CI cycle to find out if sharding worked; seeding locally would give you a faster feedback loop on the upload step specifically, at the cost of a long local build and a big upload.

Working tree is clean. Here's where things landed.

## What's fixed and already on the branch

Commit `0354edb8b` on `docs-diff-deploys` has the shape-check fix — `sort -rn | head -1` replaced with a single-pass `awk` max in [.github/workflows/docs.yml](.github/workflows/docs.yml#L259-L275). That was the actual cause of run #211's failure: the build succeeded, `head` closed the pipe, `sort` took SIGPIPE, `pipefail` turned it into exit 2, and the Netlify step never ran.

## What I tried and reverted

I implemented `assets/` sharding (256 buckets via a client-build-only Vite plugin) in [docs/.vitepress/config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts). It built cleanly and got the largest directory down from 77,915 to 257 entries. **But it breaks the site.** From VitePress's own bundle:

```js
pageClientJsFileName = `${config.assetsDir}/${pageName}.${pageHash}.lean.js`
```

VitePress hardcodes a flat `assets/<pageName>.<hash>.js` layout in both the SSR preload links and the client-side router, resolving it at runtime from a hash map. Sharded page chunks left 33 broken references on every page — SPA navigation dead. There's no config seam for this; `assetsDir` is a single static string, and a Netlify `_redirects` splat can't recompute a hash. Fully reverted, working tree clean.

(Two side effects I cleaned up: my verification build overwrote `docs/.vitepress/dist` with an English-only build — gitignored, harmless — and truncated `l10n/docs.api.pot` by 7,145 lines, which I restored.)

## The remaining decision

So `assets/` will hold ~78,000 files, and the shape check will now correctly hard-fail at 54,000. Two paths, and I'd like your call:

**A. Test the limit.** Downgrade the check from a hard fail to a warning and let Netlify be the judge. The 54,000 number is an assertion in the workflow comment from a prior session — the deploy has never actually reached Netlify, so it's never been validated. I couldn't confirm it from Netlify's docs (the URLs I tried 404'd), and I'm not willing to assert it from memory. Cost of being wrong: one ~2h CI cycle plus a failed upload.

**B. Cut the page count.** ~41.5k pages is 43 locales × the generated API tree. Excluding the machine-translated API mirrors from the deploy build would drop `assets/` well under any limit. There's already `DOCS_ROOT_LOCALE_ONLY` and `srcExclude` plumbing for exactly this shape. Cost: the translated API reference stops being published.

A is cheap and answers the question definitively; B is the guaranteed fix but gives up content. I lean A first, since B is still available afterward and we'd be making a permanent content cut on an unverified premise.

On seeding locally: still not worth it, and now it's also blocked — a local seed would hit the same directory-count question with a slower build and a 4.3 GB home upload.

content.text:
Yes — locale sharding works, and I've validated the mechanism end to end.

## What I proved

`assetsDir` is a first-class VitePress option (not the Vite one — that gets overridden) and it accepts a nested path. Built English-only with `assetsDir: "assets/en"`:

- Largest directory: `./assets/en` at 2,666 entries
- 77 asset references checked across `index.html`, `api/index.html`, and every guide page — **0 missing**
- `assets/en` is correctly baked into `chunks/theme.*.js`, so the runtime router resolves sharded page chunks
- Browser test: page renders, and client-side navigation to `/guide/getting-started` works with **zero console errors**

The enabling change is a one-liner now in [docs/.vitepress/config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts) (`DOCS_ASSETS_DIR` env override). Everything else is reverted; tree is otherwise clean.

## The catch

`__ASSETS_DIR__` is one build-time constant, so a single build can only ever write one assets directory. Locale sharding therefore means **one VitePress build per locale**, each with `assetsDir: assets/<locale>`, merged into a single `dist`. At ~967 pages per locale that's ~2–3k files per shard against a 54,000 limit — roughly 20x headroom.

This likely also fixes the *other* chronic problem: each build's working set drops to 1/43, which is what forced the 24 GB swapfile and the OOM-killer workaround. And the builds parallelize, so the 2h07m wall clock should drop substantially.

## What it costs

Four things need solving, and they're the real work:

1. **Merging outputs.** Sitemap, `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt`, and the per-locale search indexes are each generated per build and would need a merge step.
2. **Cross-locale navigation.** Each build's `__VP_HASH_MAP__` only knows its own pages, so switching locale misses the lookup. `pathToFile` returns `null` on a miss, which should degrade to a hard navigation — acceptable for a locale switch, but I haven't verified it, and that's the one behavioral risk I'd want to confirm before committing.
3. **Build orchestration.** A per-locale driver plus the merge, replacing the single `docs:build:deploy`. The diff-scoped partial-build logic in the workflow would need to become locale-aware too — though that gets *better*, since a change to one locale rebuilds only that locale.
4. **Duplicated shared chunks** across 43 locale dirs — more total bytes, but Netlify's upload is content-addressed so identical files dedupe on the wire.

Separately, I hit a real bug worth knowing about: **`vp run` doesn't pass environment variables through to the task.** `DOCS_OUT_DIR` and `DOCS_ASSETS_DIR` were both silently ignored via `vp run docs:build` and only applied under `vp exec vitepress build`. That silently invalidated my first experiment, and it'll bite the orchestration work directly since the per-locale driver depends on env passthrough.

Locale sharding works. Here's the state, including one unresolved issue.

## Validated

**Per-locale `assetsDir` solves the Netlify limit.** Built root and `hu` separately and merged:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| largest directory | 77,915 | **1,806** (`assets/root`) |
| build time | 2h07m (one build) | **32.9s + 25.9s** |

- Page scoping is exact: root emits 896 pages, hu emits 887, zero overlap
- Hash maps union cleanly — **0 key collisions** (page names are locale-prefixed), so the merged `hashmap.json` is conflict-free
- Merged `assets/` contains just `root/` and `hu/`

The build-time collapse matters as much as the file count: at ~30s per locale, 43 locales parallelize into something far below 2h, and each build's working set drops to 1/43 — which should retire the 24 GB swapfile and OOM-killer workaround entirely.

I also fixed a self-inflicted problem along the way: my first scoping attempt listed all ~40k excluded pages individually, making VitePress's per-file matching quadratic. That build took **826s**. Switching to globs brought it to 31.8s.

## Blocker

Locale scoping introduces a hydration crash:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nodeType')
  at framework.UlKvC721.js
```

I isolated it properly. It is **not** the merge (happens on the root-only build alone) and **not** my router hook (happens with the hook stashed out). It appears only once `<locale>/**` pages are excluded — the earlier `assetsDir`-only build was clean. Vue recovers by client-rendering, so the page still works, but it's a real regression. My leading suspicion is the language switcher's `correspondingLink` resolution differing between server and client when the target locale's pages aren't in the build, but I haven't confirmed that.

## Also worth flagging

Two things bit me and will bite the orchestration work:

- **`vp run` does not pass environment variables to tasks.** `DOCS_OUT_DIR` and `DOCS_ASSETS_DIR` were silently ignored; only `vp exec` honors them. This invalidated an early experiment before I caught it, and the per-locale driver depends on env passthrough.
- **Importing `../i18n.js` into the theme breaks the client bundle.** It pulls `@pantoken/i18n-engine` (`loadConfig`, filesystem) into the browser — the exact hazard `CLAUDE.md` warns about. I hit it, got `Class extends value undefined`, and rewrote the fallback to read locale keys from `ctx.siteData` instead.

## Current state

`docs/.vitepress/config.ts` (DOCS_LOCALE scoping, per-locale `assetsDir`, llms.txt gated to root) and `docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts` (cross-locale hard-navigation fallback) are modified and uncommitted. The fallback itself is written but **not yet verified** — I never got to test a cross-locale hop, because I stopped to isolate the hydration crash first.

Next step I'd take: chase the hydration crash, starting by checking whether the `hu` build crashes symmetrically. If it does, that confirms the locale switcher and points straight at `useLangs`. Want me to continue, or would you rather look at that error yourself first?

| Check | Result |
|---|---|

## The hydration crash was not mine

I built with the config and theme changes stashed out and hit the identical error on `/api/`:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nodeType')

```

- [docs/.vitepress/config.ts](docs/.vitepress/config.ts) — `DOCS_LOCALE` scoping, per-locale `assetsDir`, llms.txt gated to root
- [docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts](docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts) — cross-locale hard-navigation fallback

content.text:
It wasn't a big lift in the end — the diagnostic was the hard part, and once that landed the fix was three lines.

## What it actually was

Importing mermaid arms a `window` `load` listener that renders every element matching its default `.mermaid` selector. VitePress hydrates **after** `load` — measured on this page at load 196 ms, hydration 218 ms — so mermaid replaced the element's graph text with an SVG before Vue ever reached it.

Two fixes that look correct both fail, which is why this resisted a few attempts:

- `initialize({ startOnLoad: false })` ran inside the render function, far too late.
- Hoisting `mermaid.startOnLoad = false` to module scope does nothing either. The listener's guard reads the flag off mermaid's *internal* object, not the imported binding:

```js
function(){ if(YK.startOnLoad){ let{startOnLoad:e}=FK.getConfig(); e && YK.run()... } }
```

## The fix

Stop fighting mermaid's config and stay out of its selector. The container is now `.mermaid-diagram`, while `renderDiagram` passes the element explicitly via `nodes: [el]` — so the auto-run finds nothing regardless of config state. I also moved the first render off `watch(..., { immediate: true })` (which fires during setup, i.e. mid-hydration) onto `onMounted`.

## Verified

| | |
|---|---|
| 10 root pages incl. `/guide/architecture` | **all clean** — zero warnings, zero errors |
| Diagram | renders: 8 nodes, 7 edges, centered |
| Theme toggle | re-renders correctly (new SVG id, 8 nodes) |
| Full suite | 2,175 tests pass, coverage unchanged |

`vp check` and markdown lint clean. Diagnostic `define` removed, scratch builds cleaned up.

## What unlocked it

The decisive step was a no-rebuild experiment: swallowing `load` listeners in a Playwright init script. That both proved mermaid's auto-run was the only `load` listener on the page and showed the mismatch vanished without it — turning a guessing game into a measurement. Before that I'd been misled twice by resolving Playwright console-arg node handles *after* the fact; they're live references, so they showed post-mermaid state rather than state at warning time.
